description: The NeuralHydrology team publishes a Python library for training neural-network models of hydrological time series. Its public GitHub repository describes configuration-driven training with interchangeable datasets, model architectures, losses and optimizers on PyTorch. The repository lists the BSD 3-Clause licence, and source code is free to access. It can build streamflow models for reservoir-inflow forecasting and compare climate or catchment scenarios. The library is a modelling toolkit, not a ready-made forecast for any river basin; users must provide observations, meteorological inputs, train/test splits and their own model choices. A limitation is that model skill and transfer to ungauged catchments depend on data coverage and validation design. The cited SSP-CABra paper used this software for some daily hydrological simulations, but its results are a separate dataset. It can pair with data-brazil-ana-hidroweb-hydrometeorological-network for Brazilian observational series if inputs are prepared consistently. No package was installed or run in this review.
